source_coverage: sources/chen-2026-author/aap-chen-2025.pdf: partial, pages 1, 8 and 9 only; non-required provenance, used for the title and a visual cross-check of pages 8-9 against the PNGs

checks.claim: Lemma 20.1: finite correlated Gaussian comparison for a Banach linear image, with constant sqrt(C), all p>=1 and C=0.
checks.reason: phi(x)=||sum x_j v_j||^p is continuous and convex even for a seminorm. Z has covariance CI-Cov(xi), which is PSD, and is independent. Conditional Jensen gives E phi(xi)<=E phi(xi+Z), and xi+Z has the law of sqrt(C)g. No independence of xi_j is used. The auxiliary Z does not change the actual coupling.

checks.claim: Prop 20.2, extension and path bounds (20.3)-(20.4) on the actual Y space, using the same raw f_j and A_j.
checks.reason: Var Y(sum b_j f_j)<=C|b|^2 gives Cov<=CI for any finite orthonormal subfamily. The comparison vector has the law of the independent W(f_j) from Lemma 19.2, so tails compare exactly with ||M_M-M_N||, and M->infinity gives (20.3). N=0 gives (20.4). The limit lies in the separable closed span of the Lipschitz A_j paths. Each A_j(t) is compact by the parent results, so operator-norm limits have compact values on one event. Gaussianity follows from L^2 limits of jointly Gaussian functionals.

checks.claim: Literal row (20.5): the finite row equals Y(P_N h) and converges to Y(h), with the correct Sobolev adjoint and long intervals.
checks.reason: The coefficient identity is (19.11)/(E:driver-covariance-row) plus the raw row identity. sum_j<=N Y(f_j)<h,f_j> = Y(P_N h) by linearity on H_W. The variance bound gives L^2 convergence. G_w is exactly (17.12), with the sine sign and Bessel powers checked against S(-t)(0,f). Long intervals use the endpoint nullity and additivity of Lemma 19.8.

checks.claim: Basis independence, linearity in jointly Gaussian families, and the complexified sesquilinear form.
checks.reason: Basis independence comes from rows at rational times on dense Schwartz phases, followed by continuity. Prop 19.1 supplies the construction for any compact smooth basis. Linear combinations have a raw bound by the L^2 triangle inequality. Finite sums are linear, so path limits are too. Joint Gaussianity is the stated hypothesis. The four real-pair identities give the complex form.

checks.claim: Stability: jointly Gaussian D_n, uniform tail, fixed-head trace->0, identification M_{D_n}=M_R-M_{Y_n}, no rate restriction.
checks.reason: Cov(D_n(f_j))_{j<=N} <= s_N(n) I because a PSD matrix is bounded by its trace. Lemma 20.1 gives the head bound sqrt(s_N(n))||M_N||. The uniform C_D gives a tail independent of n. The order N then n, or the net in rho, is correct. The f_j are smooth compact tests, so the hypothesis applies to them. M_N=M_{W,N} gives the identification. The Y_n bound is redundant given the D_n bound, but harmless.

checks.claim: Lemma 20.3: physical H_Gamma with factor (2pi)^d, Schwartz inclusion, and heat C_eps with multiplier exp(-eps|xi|^2/2), defect contraction and strong limit.
checks.reason: Rechecked against Prop 16.4: B_Gamma(f,g)=int Gamma(dy) h(y), with h(y)=int f(x)g(x-y)dx. This gives (2pi)^d int hat f conj(hat g) d mu. The d=1 white case Gamma=delta_0, mu=(2pi)^{-1}d xi returns int fg. The unitary transform gives F[p*f]=c_d^{-1} hat p hat f=m_eps hat f. With 0<=m<=1 and 0<=1-m<=1, positivity, self-adjointness and both contraction bounds follow. The local bound and Schwartz cutoff argument are valid.

checks.claim: Feature space G and the exact squared isometry of Phi, with signed absolute Fubini, tensor density, closed range and the a.e. general-test formula.
checks.reason: G is real and separable. int_{-inf}^{min(t,u)} 2 lambda e^{-lambda(t+u-2r)}dr=e^{-lambda|t-u|} is correct. int nu_a(d lambda) e^{-lambda|v|}=|v|^{-a} matches author (1.21). Hence ||Phi F||_G^2=||F||_{H_W}^2 with the sqrt(2 lambda) normalization. Absolute exchanges reduce to |tau(t)sigma(u)||t-u|^{-a}, integrable since a<1. Time partitions and (19.5) give density. An isometry gives closed range. The pointwise H_Gamma limit and the a.e. G subsequence limit identify the formula. The coordinate r<0 is auxiliary and assigns no raw negative-time noise.

checks.claim: Product extension I(g)=W(Phi^-1 P g)+J((I-P)g) retains the given W and raw driver literally; the source family may use J.
checks.reason: Orthogonality and independence give E I(g)^2=||g||^2, so I is isonormal. I(Phi h)=W(h)+J(0)=W(h) is an equality of the actual variable, not only of laws. The countable basis gives one common event, so M_N and M_R are pullbacks. The text explicitly does not claim that cutoff fields are functions of W alone.

checks.claim: Exact point-feature law: finite squared norm K_eta(0)Gamma_{2eps}(0); c_d factors cancel (2pi)^d; cross covariance K_max(eta,eta')(t-s) Gamma_{eps+eps'}(x-y).
checks.reason: hat of p_eps(x-.) equals c_d e^{-i xi.x}e^{-eps|xi|^2/2}, and (2pi)^d c_d^2=1. An independent physical check by the heat semigroup gives int Gamma(dz) p_{eps+eps'}(x-y-z)=Gamma_{eps+eps'}(x-y). The common lambda range is lambda<=max(eta,eta')^{-1}. The r integral gives e^{-lambda|t-s|}. At equal parameters, K_eta(0)=eta^{-a}/(a Gamma_E(a))<infinity and Gamma_{2eps}(0)=int e^{-eps|xi|^2}d mu<infinity. Raw point noise is not evaluated.

checks.claim: The G-Bochner point-test identity is non-circular and extends to indicator tests through both raw and L^1 limits.
checks.reason: Norm continuity follows from ||v-v'||^2=2K(0)Gamma_{2eps}(0)-2K(t-s)Gamma_{2eps}(x-y), with no regularity input. int int F v = Q_rho Phi F follows from int F_t(x)p_eps(x-.)dx=C_eps F_t and the a.e. formula. L^1 convergence moves the G integrals; raw completion and the contraction move Y_rho(F_n). The forward reference to the contraction is not circular, because the contraction depends only on operator bounds.

checks.claim: Both variance dominations with constant 1, with no assumed independence of the full residual.
checks.reason: I-CP=(I-P)+P(I-C), with orthogonal lambda ranges, gives the displayed identity. The bound follows from the fiberwise contraction of I-C. ||Qg||<=||g|| is immediate. The text asserts independence only for disjoint lambda ranges and explicitly denies it for the heat residual.

checks.claim: Strong convergence Q_rho->I at arbitrary relative rates, finite L^p C^theta driver convergence, and uniform local sqrt(p)/square-exponential bounds at fixed R,T.
checks.reason: I-CP=(I-C)+C(I-P) with ||C||<=1 gives the displayed bound. Each term tends to zero independently of the other parameter. Prop 20.2's multiparameter form then gives (20.13). Constant C=1 gives ||M||_{L^p}<=||M_R||_{L^p}, and hence (19.4) uniformly in rho, including the even-moment exponential series. The conclusions are in L^p classes, with no uncountable common event.

checks.claim: Lemma 20.6: per-fixed-rho derivative features, correct heat moment, increment bound, dyadic modification, patching, and actual derivatives.
checks.reason: ||d^b v||^2=K_eta(0) int xi^{2b}e^{-eps|xi|^2}d mu carries the correct 2eps index. Next moments control difference quotients. K(0)-K(h)<=Ch from the truncated lambda range, and |e^{i xi x}-e^{i xi y}|<=|xi||x-y|, give (20.16). No density of mu is used. The dyadic estimate sqrt(q)2^{-n(1/2-m/q)} with m=d+1 is correct. Overlaps patch through countable dense sets. The FTC holds in G, is applied through I, and is enforced on rational data, then extended by continuity. The result is proved per fixed rho only.

checks.claim: Prop 20.7, statewise operator-norm Lipschitz path with only time continuity and spatial smoothness, and no norm continuity of S.
checks.reason: b_rho lies in C([0,T];C_c^k) for every k by joint continuity on a compact set. Multiplication is therefore norm continuous E_r->E_{r+1}, and S(+-u) is strongly continuous and bounded. The integrand is strongly continuous, with a sample bound giving the Lipschitz increment. E_{3/2} embeds in E_{1/2}, so the path is Lipschitz in B(E). The gain argument of Lemma 19.4 transfers exactly.

checks.claim: Prop 20.7, instantaneous duality, agreement of field and feature integrals in L^2, and equality of operator paths on the coupled space.
checks.reason: S(-u)(0,f) and the E pairing give the displayed integral with G_w at fixed u, needing only spatial smoothness. Riemann sums of the continuous field converge pathwise to the ordinary integral, and in L^2 through I to the feature integral. Time-L^2/spatial-sup approximants on common support converge both in raw norm and in L^1, so <L z,w>=Y_rho(h)=<M_R^rho z,w>. Countable phases and rational times, then boundedness and continuity, give equality on one event for fixed rho, not merely equality in law.

checks.claim: The physical mask stays after regularization and is not commuted through heat, Gamma or the free wave, and is not declared a raw-quotient multiplier.
checks.reason: b_rho=zeta_R Y_rho, and the only masked object tested is the literal class h_{R,t;z,w}. Q_rho acts in G on Phi of that class. Nothing in the section uses a multiplier on H_W, which is consistent with the obstruction in Prop 16.5.

checks.claim: Source fidelity: heat (1.20), Laplace (1.21), self law (2.9), joint law (2.11); page 9 not used as given-W retention; page 8 index neither imported nor silently repaired; citation matches.
checks.reason: PNG p5 (1.20) is p(t,x)=(2 pi t)^{-d/2}exp(-|x|^2/2t). PNG p6 (1.21) is |u|^{-alpha0}=Gamma(alpha0)^{-1} int_0^inf e^{-lambda|u|} d lambda/lambda^{1-alpha0}. PNG p8 (2.9) has truncation delta^{-1} and gamma_{2 eps}. PNG p9 (2.11) has gamma^0_{delta v delta~} and gamma_{eps+eps~}. All match (20.6), (20.10) and (20.11), with the rename delta->eta. Page 8's increment display indeed shows gamma_eps(0) and gamma_eps(x-y), against 2eps in (2.9). The text flags this and derives (20.16) independently. Page 9 says 'Without changing its distribution', and the text treats it as law-only. The extra.bib key, line, title and SHA agree with the pin, and PDF p1 confirms title and author.

checks.reason: All formulas (20.1)-(20.17) were compared with the TeX and rendered text. Cross-references resolve correctly by counting parents: Prop 19.1, (19.1), (19.5), (17.12), Prop 16.4, Lemmas 19.4, 19.8, 19.9, Prop 20.2, Lemma 20.3, Lemma 20.4. Seven proofs each end with the required 'This proves' sentence. No clipping or overlap was seen; (20.9)'s number sits on its own line by design.

checks.claim: Correspondence with accepted da9d464 Sections 1-7, including the five adopted clarifications, without hidden strength change.
checks.reason: Every step in the md has a TeX counterpart. The a.e. formula, direct continuity, nested rectangles and J-dependence wording are all present. The projection-letter item stays cosmetic. The TeX regularity statement on compact rectangles implies the md's compact cones. The only compressions are expository, such as the Cauchy construction by reference to Lemma 19.9.

checks.claim: Scope preservation: full H:homog (d=1,2,3, Radon/singular/white, alpha=d=1), zero case, amplitudes, and fixed R,T; no nonlinear, canonical-solution or moment claim.
checks.reason: Hypothesis 1.1 is retained, and no density or evaluation of a Sobolev displacement is used. Gamma=0 is trivial as stated. The closing paragraph keeps Young flow, initial datum (1,0) and moment transfer separate. No uniform-R, Skorohod, companion or whole-paper clearance appears in the section.

minor: Non-mandatory. integrated_source_convergence.tex lines 250 and 286, rendered p145-146: the width symbol in Gamma_e and p_e is the letter e, so the display reads e^{-e|xi|^2/2}, with the same glyph as the exponential base. The formula is correct but typographically ambiguous; a different width letter would be cleaner.

Non-mandatory. Lines 13-15 write A_j(t) and M_N for the objects Prop 19.1 calls A_j(0,t) and X_N, without stating the identification. The meaning is unambiguous and no proof depends on the difference.

Non-mandatory. Lines 98-103 cite no label for the coefficient identity; (E:driver-covariance-row) with (E:driver-raw-row) would be the pointer. Lines 65 and 454 use v_z and [S(u)z]_1 without pointing to (E:variance-displacement). I checked both identifications directly.

Non-mandatory. Lines 317-319 compress two routine identifications: the H_Gamma Bochner integral of heat translates equals the Schwartz test p_eps*F_t (Riemann sums converge in Schwartz seminorms), and the G Bochner integral equals its pointwise formula a.e. (pair with simple functions). Both are valid; expansion is optional.

Non-mandatory. Lemma 20.6 does not name the time domain of its rectangles. The '1/2 power at small distances' wording is stronger than needed, because |x-y|<=C|x-y|^{1/2} holds on any compact rectangle. Only [0,T] is consumed by Prop 20.7, and the feature is well defined at every real t.

Non-mandatory. Line 434 writes 'L_rho=M_R^rho for all t' with the time argument suppressed. Line 484 uses workflow vocabulary ('pinned'), which is better replaced in final paper prose. Gamma_E is used without a local reminder of its Section 16 definition. These are presentation only.

Non-mandatory, provenance only. worker-honesty-v1.md line 11 says '80facts22seams', while source-operator-convergence.md line 466 and the 2026-10-30 adjudication say '71facts/18seams'. The dates differ, and neither count is used by the section, so this may be chronological. I did not adjudicate it; it has no scientific effect on this section.
findings.mandatory_status: All seven minor findings are non-mandatory. No finding blocks acceptance.

limitations: This is an AI scientific review, not human verification or a novelty audit.

No hash, build, Git, Lean, numeric or script execution was performed. The SHA values, the 150-page clean build, the 93 unchanged old proof bodies and the C0 scan in build-v1.json and worker-honesty-v1.md are author claims, which I did not independently run.

The PDF is non-required provenance. I viewed only pages 1, 8 and 9: pages 8-9 agree visually with the supplied PNGs, and page 1 confirms title and author. Pages 5 and 6 were checked only through the supplied PNGs, and no full-book audit was done. The PDF's own hash was not computed.
The bibliography render of reference [4] is not on the supplied pages. Citation agreement was checked from the key, extra.bib, author-pin-v1.json and the citation as rendered on p141.
Parent Sections 16-19 were reused as accepted evidence with each new application rechecked. Their full proofs were read but not re-adjudicated line by line, and their constants are inherited.

The result is limited to local linear Gaussian source drivers at fixed finite R,T. It gives no clearance for nonlinear Young flow, initial datum (1,0), canonical u, moment transfer or asymptotics, Skorohod, uniform-R, companion or public delivery, or whole-paper or cold-read status.
